correctness.rationale: For q>=3, a length-h linear window within distinct letter runs can have a repeated Parikh profile only for consecutive starts; its shift transition count is the linear window formula. For circular windows, proper support determines first/last runs or a single-run contiguous plateau, and full-alphabet support can be reduced to a complementary window missing a letter, proving the analogous circular contiguity lemma. Thus distinct cyclic Parikh profiles equal unequal adjacent-window shift count, computed from same-letter overlaps in runs; length blocks of P^k consist of k-1 full circular sets and one terminal linear set. Summing finite overlap formulas gives p+(2k-1)S+(k-1), including k=1 and full-length h=p. Independent literal factor-set enumeration matched all 11,856 length profiles across 723 finite instances; proof handles every allowed run length.
